text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased paging and KV cache growth on runtime-pool-3. Error rate on streaming endpoints increased. Paging rate up 4x. Triggering paging_threshold_alert (p95 paging latency > 200ms)

oncall-bot: Automated mitigation suggestions: fallback to model-variant 'small-kv', throttle continuous-batching, or increase eviction aggressiveness.

eli: seeing huge bump in kv_cache.size on pod runtime-3-7: 1.1GB -> 9.8GB in ~6m. Streaming responses are stuttering / partial flushes. Repro locally with long convo + streaming=true.

maya: i think this is related to yesterday's runtime tweak: `continuous_batching.max_tokens_per_batch` was increased from 64 -> 256 in the rollout at ~1910123000. @samir did that land in prod?

samir: yeah i rolled the config change in canary then promoted. it reduced throughput a bit but didn't show regressions on unit tests. i didn't run long-tail streaming tests.

lisa: logs show a pattern of repeated KV cache misses that expand keys due to unbounded prefix indexing. snippet from runtime logs (pod runtime-3-7):

```
[2026-03-15T02:03:12Z] kv_cache.insert key_prefix='user:convo:abc123:' size_delta=+64000 total=1123456
[2026-03-15T02:03:13Z] kv_cache.insert key_prefix='user:convo:abc123:' size_delta=+128000 total=2403456
[2026-03-15T02:03:16Z] paging: write 128k -> ssd queue (throttle=off)
[2026-03-15T02:04:21Z] streaming: partial_flush triggered (tokens_sent=23, expected_continuation=true)
```

eli: partial_flush = the token cadence optimization is emitting partial frames and then stalling because the KV cache insert slowed the serving thread; streaming queue starves -> clients see truncated responses.

ops-runner: customer reports: two customers (acct: acme-inc, acct: libre-saas) observed truncated streams and reconnects ~02:03-02:12 UTC. We have a few 500s and 504s. Ticket created: INC-9421.

maya: mitigation proposal: 1) revert continuous_batching.max_tokens_per_batch to 64 (previous) 2) enable aggressive eviction for kv cache: `kv_eviction.rate=10MB/s` 3) temporarily disable streaming cadence optimization by toggling `STREAMING_CADENCE=false` 4) throttle new streaming connections at edge for 10m. Which is fastest?

samir: fastest is toggle STREAMING_CADENCE and throttle edge. revert of config needs rollout but okay. i'll push cadence toggle first.

eli: do the cadence toggle and eviction increase now. i'll prepare rollback for the batching change.

samir: running command to flip cadence flag on runtime-pool-3 (rolling):
```
kubectl -n prod set env ds/runtime-cadence runtime-cadence=disabled --selector=pool=runtime-pool-3
```

samir: flipped on three pods so far, latency on those pods for streaming recovered to normal in ~40s. paging writes dropped by ~70% on those targets. :thumbsup:

lisa: eviction rate bump applied via config API: `POST /admin/runtime/config` payload `{ \"kv_eviction\": { \"rate\": \"10MB/s\" } }` -> accepted. paging queue drained.

ops-runner: throttling new streaming connections at edge (rate-limit 5rps per customer) via api-gw rule id: gw-2981.

customer-sre-bot: Notifying impacted customers: email sent to acme-inc and libre-saas outlining mitigation and asking for logs if they still see issues.

eli: rolling back continuous_batching.max_tokens_per_batch now. this requires config rollout across pools. starting with runtime-pool-3 canary subset (pods 3-7). command: `PATCH /admin/runtime/config continuous_batching.max_tokens_per_batch=64`

samir: patch queued, starting rollout. will monitor KV size and paging metrics.

lisa: dashboard snapshots:
- before: kv_cache_total=9.8GB, paging_rate=420 ops/s, streaming_500s=4.2%
- after toggles: kv_cache_total=1.6GB, paging_rate=90 ops/s, streaming_500s=0.6%

ops-runner: customer impact summary for oncall handoff: two customers had degraded streaming with reconnects and truncated outputs for ~9-12 minutes. no data loss, no secrets exposed. SLO hit: p99 latency for streaming spiked above SLO for ~10 min.

eli: adding follow-ups: (1) write an automated long-tail streaming regression test that includes KV cache stress with prefix churn, (2) revert batching default until test coverage, (3) add a guardrail to cap `continuous_batching.max_tokens_per_batch` to 128, (4) add alert for partial_flush rate > 0.5% per cluster.

maya: i'll open a PR with the guardrail and test plan. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for visibility.

samir: handing off to next oncall @maya for midnight shift. things are stable for now. watchlist: kv_cache_total, paging_rate, partial_flush_rate for next 2 hours. escalation: ping @eli if partial_flush_rate > 0.5% or paging_rate > 200 ops/s.

maya: oncall ack, will monitor dashboards. noted follow-ups and will coordinate postmortem.

ops-runner: post-incident items logged in INC-9421: root cause: config promotion of continuous_batching parameter without long-tail streaming validation -> unbounded prefix expansion in KV cache -> paging surge -> streaming partial flush / token cadence stalls. mitigation: cadence toggle, eviction bump, rate limits, rollback. next steps include guardrails and tests.

customer-sre-bot: follow-up emails will include a timeline and mitigations. customers offered 1 week of advanced support credits.

eli: quick note for postmortem: include the exact config diff, rollout time, and who approved the promotion. also attach the runtime traces for the partial_flush events.

maya: copying incident to #postmortems and assigning owner for the write-up (samir).

samir: i'll own the write-up. target: draft within 48h.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. thread closed for active mitigation. If any new anomalies => reopen. :white_check_mark:
